passage:
For history class, students created a small museum in their classroom. Each student brought one old object from home and wrote a label for it.
There were coins, toys, photos, bowls, letters, and tools. One student brought an old bus ticket from his grandmother. Another brought a radio that no longer worked.
Visitors walked around the classroom and read the labels. They learned not only about objects, but also about families.
The teacher said, "A museum does not begin with glass boxes. It begins with attention."
Students returned the objects carefully after the project. They looked at their homes differently afterward. Ordinary things could become history when someone asked their stories.
